note: v4: a lead (lead-tape) comes down the scale two octaves over the tune's last six bars (0:57-1:12), onto the low F where the guitars' run begins: the one line in the song that really moves
v7: the turn's third cycle (1:36-1:46) is heard naked (no snare, china or bass: the chug and its kick); the fourth has the kit back on the backbeat with the china in eighths

v8: from the tune's third statement (0:48) the right side's four guitars play it two scale steps higher (thirds and fourths over the left), each side under its own bell; it holds under the lead to the run at 1:12

v9: the fall steepens: two steps of the scale a bar from bar 60 (2:24), three from 66, six in 68-70 (a step on each accent of the riff), then the run; first cut (four a bar) read as a saw-tooth and was recut
v17: on the last F at 4:12 the guitars release the lower strings. F2 and C3 remain at nearly the old loudness; the low F is left to the ear.
v20: at 0:09.6 the first hats count four quick bars in three real ones; from 0:16.8 they count the original pulse into the tom fill. Guitars and tone unchanged.
v21: at 2:24 the right guitars climb the six notes while the left and the basses keep falling, two steps a bar; they meet on F at 2:31 and 2:38.4.

v22, 1:50.4–1:55.2: under the turn's last two bars a roll on the song's own tom really speeds up, from sixteenths to 43 strokes a second, the frequency of the low F, so the roll becomes a rising note that arrives on the descent's bar line. One new track; nothing else moves.
v23, the fill that never tops out: the falling toms go UP into the lead at 0:57.6 (eight strokes) and at its octave, 1:04.8 (twelve); the crashes follow the lead in threes

v24, 0:48.0–0:56.4: where the right side goes into harmony the backbeat doubles (the snare on the 'and' of every beat, four to the bar), the kit's third gear under the stair; at 0:57.6, where the lead comes in, it drops back. Only the snare changes.
v29: the china leaves the bar and goes with the guitars' three speeds (a Risset rhythm on one cymbal, 95 strokes -> 400); snare, bass and crashes keep the clock. C10T5_TAPE='' = v28.
v30 HALF WAY ROUND: under the three leads the plain tone holds F, then B, a bar each, for the pole's ten bars (2:52.8-3:16.8): a stair with two steps, half an octave each. C10T5_HALFWAY='' = v29.

v32: the turn climbs the stair (1:26.4-1:55.2). Each time the turn comes round the chug and the bass are a step up the stair's line (G flat, A flat, B), then the descent drops back to F. Nothing moves in time. The window's 'static in tone' flag is gone (motion 0.0594 > 0.0930). Card fs-turn-climb asks whether the speed illusion survives the steps.

v34: the fall's steepest two bars (2:43.2-2:48.0, six steps a bar): both stairs at once and the two sides change places from step to step (Deutsch's scale illusion): the left plays F Gb C B Ab Eb, the right F Eb Ab B C Gb; nobody plays the fall or the climb; basses, tone and kit keep the fall
